slides.title: 4 order types every trader must know.
slides.text: Using the wrong one costs money on **every** trade.

points.b: Fills now, at the best available price
points.t: Speed is guaranteed. The price is not.
In fast markets you can fill worse than the price you saw.

points.b: Fills at your price or better
points.t: Buy limit below the market, sell limit above it.
If price never reaches it, you're not in the trade.

points.b: Becomes a market order at your price
points.t: Used for stop losses and breakout entries.
In a gap or a spike it fills beyond the stop.

points.b: Becomes a limit order at your price

points.t: A stop-limit used as a stop loss may never fill.

slides.title: Your stop loss should be a stop order.
slides.text: A stop-limit can be skipped in a fast move. That's exactly when you need to be out.

post.instagram:
Market: fills now, price not guaranteed. Limit: your price or better, fill not guaranteed. Stop: becomes a market order at your price, used for stop losses. Stop-limit: becomes a limit order, and can be skipped in a fast move, so don't use it as your protective stop.
